current_status.to: Active as of 2026-07-31; the moratorium remains the operative instrument, and permanent replacement regulations are still in draft form. Per the Franklin County Area Plan Commission's own July 8, 2026 meeting agenda, 'Moratorium - Update (Data Centers)' remained an item under Unfinished Business, with the next APC meeting calendared for 2026-08-12. The county's posted Data Center Regulations draft (Section 80.06.09) had reached only 'v.4.0', issued 2026-06-22, and is explicitly marked 'a working draft ... It does not carry the force of law.' A May 13, 2026 public hearing gathered comments that the work group was still incorporating as of the June 22 draft.
current_status.reason: Direct review of the Area Plan Commission's own posted agenda (July 8, 2026) and the draft ordinance's own cover sheet (version 4.0, June 22, 2026) confirms no permanent ordinance has been adopted as of this research date; the moratorium therefore remains accurate as 'extended'/active.

outcome.to: The Data Center Moratorium Work Group and APC advanced the draft ordinance to v4.0 (dated 2026-06-22) following a May 13, 2026 public hearing that produced roughly 25 public comments; the item remained on the APC's unfinished-business agenda as of the July 8, 2026 meeting, with the next meeting calendared for August 12, 2026. No final adoption vote by the APC or Board of Commissioners has been confirmed as of 2026-07-31.
outcome.reason: Updates the drafting timeline with the most recent version and meeting record found.

The permanent ordinance process has progressed (four draft versions, a May 13, 2026 public hearing) but had not reached adoption as of the July 8, 2026 APC meeting, the most recent primary-source meeting record available. Recommend checking the August 12, 2026 APC meeting outcome in a follow-up pass.

evidence.title: Indy councilors advance data center moratorium with Hogsett's backing
evidence.supports: Confirms a City-County Council committee advanced a data center moratorium proposal 10-3 on July 13, 2026, sponsored by Council President Maggie Lewis, proposed to run through the end of 2027, with Mayor Hogsett's support and requiring further full-Council and Metropolitan Development Commission approval before taking effect; also notes previously approved projects and complete applications would be unaffected.
evidence.quote: I support the proposed data center moratorium and welcome the additional time to continue this vital conversation.

evidence.title: Data center rules proposal clears initial vote in Indianapolis
evidence.supports: Confirms a related but distinct permanent data-center zoning ordinance cleared an initial 5-3 Metropolitan Development Commission vote on July 1, 2026, with final approval by the full City-County Council not expected until August 2026 -- a separate track from the Council-driven moratorium proposal.
evidence.quote: The ordinance is intended to regulate where data centers can be built in Marion County, how close they can sit to homes and how much noise they can generate.

new_candidates.notes: Two parallel Indianapolis/Marion County tracks are underway: (1) a permanent data-center zoning ordinance via the Metropolitan Development Commission (initial vote 5-3 on 2026-07-01; full Council approval expected August 2026), and (2) a separate Council-driven moratorium (committee-approved 10-3 on 2026-07-13, proposed through end of 2027) intended to pause new approvals while (1) is finalized. Neither had completed final enactment as of 2026-07-31. This is a jurisdiction not currently in the Indiana inventory; recommend tracking both threads in the next research pass.
